version.changelog: Fix: ensure full API database file is included

llm.summary: The skill's code and README largely match the claimed purpose (Virtuoso Skill API lookup + linting), but there are multiple implementation inconsistencies and hardcoded paths that warrant caution before running it.

dimensions.detail: The scripts and SKILL.md implement API search, linting, and a simple chatbot/web UI which matches the declared purpose. However there are mismatches: the chatbot defaults to loading 'skill_api_database.json' while the repository provides references/skill_api_database.json; the linter expects 'skill_api_database_full.json' which is not present in the manifest; some scripts mention very different API counts (manifest/README list ~312 functions, skill_lint refers to '10124' in its docstring). These filename and count inconsistencies suggest sloppy packaging or leftover artifacts from edits — not necessarily malicious, but incoherent and likely to cause runtime errors.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md only instructs running the included scripts (chatbot, lint). The scripts will read local files and directories you point them at (expected for a linter), and the web mode starts a Flask server to expose search functionality. That behavior is consistent with the declared purpose, but two concerns: (1) scripts contain hardcoded absolute paths (e.g. /root/.openclaw/qqbot/downloads/...) in extraction utilities — these are host-specific and could leak developer assumptions; (2) running the linter with a directory argument will read any files under that directory (including sensitive files if you mistakenly point it at a system path). The SKILL.md does not declare the Flask dependency explicitly in the registry metadata.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No external install spec is provided (instruction-only + included scripts), so nothing is automatically downloaded or executed by an installer. This reduces install-time risk. Note: the chatbot's web mode requires Flask (the script prints a hint to pip install flask), but that dependency is not declared in registry metadata.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables, no credentials, and no config paths in the manifest. The code likewise does not read env vars or attempt network authentication. This is proportionate to the stated functionality. The remaining concern is hardcoded file paths in helper scripts which reference a root user's download path; these are not credential requests but indicate leftover local paths.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true and does not request any elevated or persistent platform privileges. It doesn't attempt to modify other skills or system-wide agent settings. Web mode opens a local HTTP server if you run it, which is an explicit action by the user.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to implement the claimed API lookup and linting features, but has several packaging and path inconsistencies. Before running it: (1) inspect the included JSON database files (references/skill_api_database.json) and confirm which filename the scripts expect (or copy/rename the DB to the expected names: skill_api_database.json and/or skill_api_database_full.json); (2) review the scripts for any hardcoded absolute paths (e.g. /root/.openclaw/...) and remove or change them; (3) run the linter or chatbot only on directories/files you trust — the linter will read any files you point it at; (4) if you enable the web mode, bind it to localhost or run it behind a firewall and install Flask only from a trusted source (pip install flask) after reviewing the code that handles HTTP requests; (5) prefer to run the tools in a sandbox or VM until you confirm they behave as expected. These inconsistencies look like sloppy packaging rather than deliberate malice, but exercise caution because the code will read local files and run a web server if invoked.
